name: Fomes fomentarius

tip_speed.source: Dresch et al. 2015, Fungal strain matters: colony growth and bioactivity of the European medicinal polypores Fomes fomentarius, Fomitopsis pinicola and Piptoporus betulinus, AMB Express 5:4
tip_speed.note: malt extract agar, 9 cm plates, 25 to 30 C. Three Austrian strains reached a mean colony diameter of 7.0 to 8.1 cm (5 mm plug already subtracted) in 7 days: 5.0 to 5.8 mm/day radial, midpoint 5.4 mm/day x 41.7. The plates were close to full, so this is a lower bound. A fourth strain reached only 5 cm (3.6 mm/day); an Italian strain reached 8.7 cm at 32 C

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.source: Dresch et al. 2015, Fungal strain matters: colony growth and bioactivity of the European medicinal polypores Fomes fomentarius, Fomitopsis pinicola and Piptoporus betulinus, AMB Express 5:4
t_opt.note: optimum for four of five strains (Austria) on malt extract agar, tested at 10, 20, 25, 30, 32, 37 C; the one Italian strain was fastest at 32 C. Kim & Chai 2004 (J. Mushrooms 2(4):200-206, abstract) give 30 C and growth from about 10 to 30 C for a Korean strain

size_cm.source: First Nature (P. O'Reilly), Fomes fomentarius, Hoof Fungus / Tinder Fungus, species page
size_cm.note: bracket width; up to 20 cm deep at the attachment. Field-guide web page, not a monograph

notes: A weak parasite and then a saprotroph that forms a decay column inside the trunk. Reported (unchecked) to be cold-hardy, with a fruit body that adds a layer each year for decades.
